incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV cache size spike detected on serving-cluster-3. Growth rate > 15GB/min for 3 consecutive minutes. Error rate on text-generation endpoints increased ~8%. Paging oncall: @Jordan (oncall).

Jordan (oncall): Picking this up. Thanks bot. Which model pools are affected? Any correlated deploys?

Maya R.: I see the spike coinciding with a speculative-decoding feature rollout this morning (canary). Metrics show continuous-batching queue length also increased. Hypothesis: speculative decoding is causing additional cache writes per draft that aren't being deduped, causing cache blowups.

Alex G.: Confirmed. Traces show many KV.set ops per request where before we had 1-2 sets. Example trace: `speculative:draft.v2 -> write(kv_key_<session>, size=12KB)`, repeated for multiple drafts.

Jordan (oncall): Ok mitigation plan: 1) Pause speculative decoding feature for canary/hosted. 2) Apply hotfix to batching config to limit max_batch_tokens and aggressive cache pruning. 3) Roll traffic to safer model variant if needed. Can someone assemble the exact commands?

Taylor S.: Working on rollback patch. For pause we can flip `speculative.enabled=false` in feature config service for canary tag, and restart workers in the canary pool. Command (canary pool):

```
# feature flag flip
redwood feature flip speculative-decoding --env=prod --tag=canary --value=false
# restart canary workers
kubectl -n serving rollout restart ds/serving-canary
```

Alex G.: For batch config hotfix, propose: reduce max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 512, set max_batch_size from 64 -> 16, and enable kv_cache_soft_limit=80%. Patch snippet:

```
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 512
  max_batch_size: 16
  batch_timeout_ms: 8
kv_cache:
  enabled: true
  soft_limit_percent: 80
  eviction_policy: lru
```

Maya R.: Add an extra safety: throttle speculative write path at runtime so each request tops out at N drafts (N=1) until we confirm cache correctness. I can push a small guard patch to the runtime.

Jordan (oncall): Apply steps in order. Taylor, flip flag + restart. Alex, patch batching config and deploy as hotfix to canary then prod if stable. Maya, guard patch in parallel. I'll monitor memory and request error graphs.

Taylor S.: Flag flipped and canary workers restarted. `feature flip` returned success. Observability shows initial drop in new KV writes for canary pool.

devops-bot: Deploy status: rollout of canary restart succeeded (3/3 pods ready).

Alex G.: Hotfix applied to canary batching config and rolled. Logs showing batch sizes reduced. Early signal: KV write rate down ~70% on canary.

Maya R.: Guard patch pushed to runtime (branch: runtime/kv-guard). Applied via immediate patch to canary with dynamic flag `speculative.draft_limit=1`.

Jordan (oncall): Good. Monitoring: total KV cache size growth rate dropped to ~1GB/min cluster-wide, error rate trending down. However, we still see residual large cache entries from earlier period. Need a controlled prune.

Alex G.: I can run an eviction job to prune keys matching the speculative draft prefix older than 1h. Plan: dry-run list -> verify -> delete. Command: `python tools/kv_prune.py --prefix speculative:draft --older-than 1h --dry-run`

Taylor S.: Approved. Run dry-run first and post sample key count.

Alex G.: Dry-run results: would remove ~420k keys (~14GB). Will proceed with staged deletes on low-traffic nodes first, then ramp.

Jordan (oncall): Execute staged prune, throttle deletions to avoid overload (5000 keys/min per node). Keep me posted.

Alex G.: Deletion started on nodes 1-3. Progress: 25% done. No spike in error rates.

devops-bot: KV prune job running (job-id kv-prune-2024-06-13-09).

Maya R.: Note for postmortem: need to investigate draft vs target caching semantics. Current speculative flow writes drafts into the same KV namespace without clear versioning which makes dedup/eviction tricky. We should consider draft-scoped keys or mark with ttl.

Jordan (oncall): Agree. For now, continue prune then plan a longer-term change: namespace draft keys, add TTL 30m, and add a guard to not write identical KV entries across speculative drafts.

Taylor S.: Handoff: I'm going offline in ~25m. Jordan, do you want me to stay for verification after prune completes?

Jordan (oncall): If you can, stay until prune completes; otherwise I'll pick up. Paging rotation note: @Maya R. you are on-call for the next shift, I'll follow up with summary in #eng-oncall-handoffs.

Taylor S.: I'll stay. Prune at 60% now, nodes stable.

Alex G.: Prune complete across all targeted nodes. Total reclaimed: 14.2GB. No additional client errors observed. KV cache size back to baseline.

devops-bot: All canary services reporting healthy.

Jordan (oncall): All mitigations succeeded. Next steps: 1) Revert temporary aggressive batching limits after 24h of stability to avoid perf regressions. 2) Implement draft namespace + TTL and dedup logic in runtime. 3) Add integration tests to catch speculative write multiplication. 4) Postmortem and customer impact assessment.

Maya R.: I'll own the runtime change and tests (ETA 2 weeks). I'll also prepare an eval that simulates speculative drafts load to validate.

Taylor S.: I'll revert the batching limits in 24h if no regressions.

Jordan (oncall): Customer impact assessment: Incident affected a subset of hosted customers on the canary/hosted pools for ~45 minutes. Increased p95 latency by ~250ms and error-rate spike up to 8% briefly. No data exfiltration. We'll notify CS with summary.

Maya R.: Adding a note: speculative decoding interacts badly with KV cache when multiple draft paths share keys — root cause: draft/target sync bug where draft keys are indistinguishable. Postmortem will detail.

Taylor S.: Thanks team. Posting incident thread to #postmortems once we have the writeup. :thumbsup:

Jordan (oncall): Handoff complete. Final status: resolved, mitigations applied, root-cause investigation ongoing. Closing pager.

incident-bot: Pager closed by Jordan (oncall). Duration: 52m.
